synergies.why: "Once each turn, when an enemy unit dies while I'm at a battlefield, play a Gold gear token exhausted" keys on an actual death, and 428.1 defines Killing as a Permanent going to the Trash from the board. 808.1.d and 808.1.d.1 — written for Deathknell, but stating the same event — say outright that when a "killed" event is replaced by anything else (their own worked example is a recall), the death never happened and the trigger is stripped from the chain before it fires. So Pyke only pairs with the members of this family that actually put the enemy in the Trash: the damage-based removal spells (including the two mutual-damage spells, which can kill the enemy side of the exchange) and the two unconditional Kill instructions. The bounce, the steal-and-recall, the deck-return, the banish-or-bounce and the banish-that-replaces-death all empty the battlefield just as well for the ENGINE this family already stands on (possession-action-defender-flip, sinister-poro-attack-evacuate), but none of them ever pays Pyke.

synergies.name: Portal Rescue replays a body for free, off the board instead of out of hand

excludes.why: the predicate caught "play a non-token gear" in his trigger condition; his play effect readies something, it puts nothing on the board.

synergies.why: "Banish a friendly unit, then its owner plays it to their base, ignoring its cost" is a third enabler of the same shape retreat-replays-a-body and pack-of-wonders-replays-a-body already stand on, and a stronger one: 419.3 / 419.3.a / 419.3.b treat this forced replay as an ordinary Play ("Treat all steps of Play as normal"), so 419.4.a fires the unit's own "When you play me" trigger a second time exactly as a hand-replay does, and 355.2.a already lists the controller's Base among the default valid locations the card sends it to. Unlike Retreat (which only returns the body to hand, so the second cast still costs its full price) and Pack of Wonders (same, plus it needs another gear or unit to spend a card on), Portal Rescue banishes straight off the board and replays "ignoring its cost" in the same breath — one card buys a completely free second play effect, at [Action] speed, so it reaches the opponent's Showdowns as well as your own Main Phase.

synergies.name: Drag an enemy onto your own battlefield and Teemo's Defend Trigger fires on your turn

partner.textMatches: [Mm]ove (up to \w+ |any number of |all |a |an )?enemy units?|choose an opponent\. They move a unit they control to the same battlefield

excludes.why: "When I attack, you may move any number of enemy units here each with 5 Might or less to their base" fires on Corrupted Dragon's own attack and sends the enemy to its BASE, never to a battlefield — 450 needs the destination to be a Battlefield for Contested to apply, so this clears a path for an attack instead of luring anyone in.

Imposing Challenger pushes the enemy AWAY to "a different battlefield", not toward one the mover controls; its own established use (faefolk-challenger-forced-attacker) un-stages the Combat he is already in via 323.10, the opposite mechanism from creating Contested at a battlefield you already garrison.
Isolate sends the enemy unit to its own base. A base is never a Battlefield, so 450 never applies and no Contested status is created — this is removal, not a lure.
Janna's optional move sends the enemy unit "from here to its base" — the same base destination as Isolate, so 450 is never met.

Sinister Poro moves the enemy unit to ITS base, and its own catalogued combo (sinister-poro-attack-evacuate) uses exactly that to clear the Defender for a bloodless win on your own attack — the opposite direction from luring one onto your battlefield.
Stare Down moves the enemy units at the chosen battlefield to their own base. Base is not a Battlefield, so 450 never applies here either.

Temptation moves the enemy unit "to a location where there's a unit with the same controller" — toward the opponent's OWN board, never onto a battlefield the mover controls, so it can never apply Contested against them (190.3.a.1).

synergies.why: Teemo, Strategist's "When I defend" ability (383.4.f) only fires when the opponent chooses to attack his battlefield, which a player who has seen him simply stops doing. 190.3.a / 190.3.a.1 key the Contested status on the MOVED unit's controller, not on whoever caused the move, and 450 makes the destination Contested whenever it is a Battlefield "not controlled by the controller of the Unit or Units that moved" — so dragging (or forcing) an enemy unit onto a battlefield you already control makes THEM the Attacker (464.2.c.1) and every friendly unit standing there, Teemo included, the Defender (464.2.c.2, 464.2.c.3) on YOUR OWN turn. Several of these cards name no destination at all (Charm, Skyward Strike, Dragon's Rage, Tricksy Tentacles, Blast Cone); 355.4 / 355.4.a let the controller of the Move Effect pick any valid location, including a battlefield they already hold, which is exactly how teemo-strategist-rabadons-deathcrown-bonus-kill already uses Charm and teemo-strategist-swift-scout-hidden-flood already uses Evelynn, Entrancing. UNL-101 Call to Battle is a fourth, unique shape in the family: instead of you choosing which enemy unit moves, it forces the OPPONENT to send one of their own — 190.3.a.1 keys on the moved unit's controller regardless of who chose the move, so the effect is identical.

synergies.name: Dark Child pays for a Reaction unit on the opponent's turn
synergies.why: The same mechanism as dark-child-off-turn-reactions, for the other card type bare [Reaction] appears on. 813.1.b/813.1.c.1 do not distinguish a spell from a unit — either can be played during a Closed State on any player's turn — and playing a unit costs the same Energy/Power a spell does, which is exactly what Dark Child's two readied runes (164.2.a's Reaction-speed Seal abilities) pay for. Only 3 printings in the whole pool carry BARE [Reaction] on a unit (not [Ambush]'s different reminder, "You may play me as a [Reaction] to a battlefield where you have units," and not a gear or legend's own exhaust-activated [Reaction] ability): Shen, Kinkou; Rengar, Pouncing; Janna, Savior. All three print the longer unit reminder — "...including to a battlefield you control" — which the predicate's exact-phrase match uses to stay off [Ambush] and off activated abilities entirely.

synergies.name: Scrutinizing Sergeant is a flat XP tax nobody has to spend to trigger
synergies.why: Scrutinizing Sergeant gains 1 XP per friendly unit on play with no [Hunt] and no [Level] of its own, so it falls outside both existing XP rules — gardens-of-becoming-xp is anchored on a SPENDER and hunts other spend/pay text, blood-rose-level hunts other [Level N] text — neither one's partner predicate reads a plain producer as a partner of itself, and this rule is the missing anchor-direction: a producer paired with anything that spends or checks XP. 730.1/730.2 make XP a trackable, spendable resource regardless of source, so what feeds a spend threshold does not have to be [Hunt] or [Level] text.

synergies.name: Magma Wurm lets a whole turn of token bodies attack the turn they land
synergies.why: 143.4 defaults every unit that enters the board to exhausted; Magma Wurm's static "Other friendly units enter ready" overrides that default for everything you play while she is out, not just herself. Nothing in the pool pays this off one unit at a time — the payoff scales with how many bodies land in the same turn, which is exactly what a unit-token generator does (per #48's walk-to-the-battlefield finding, the bottleneck on a token swarm was never the count, it was getting them anywhere useful; Magma Wurm removes the other bottleneck, needing to wait a turn to attack). One-shot per token batch, no repeat step of its own, so this is a deckbuilding pairing rather than an engine.

synergies.name: Weaponmaster re-equips an Equipment you already control for a rune less
synergies.why: [Weaponmaster]'s own reminder text — "you may [Equip] one of your Equipment to me for a rune less, even if it's already attached" — is a discount on the [Equip] Activated Ability (818.1), independent of aphelios-equipment-attach's per-attach mode choice: this is a second, independent equip-discount mechanism, not a rewording of the first. It cannot loop: 818.1 makes Equip an Activated Ability, so re-equipping is never Playing (818.1.b) and never re-fires a "When you play this" on the gear or a second copy of Weaponmaster's own "When you play me" trigger — "even if it's already attached" only changes WHERE the Equipment ends up, once, on the turn Weaponmaster enters.

synergies.name: A deck that keeps its own rune count low turns on six payoffs at once

partner.textMatches: fewer runes than an opponent|control 4 or fewer runes

synergies.why: Six Vendetta cards share one of two clauses keyed to a LOW rune count: "fewer runes than an opponent" (Forsaken Baccai, Oasis Raider) or "4 or fewer runes" (Baccai Sandspinner, Eclipse Dragon, Renekton Rage Fueled, and the battlefield Protective Sands) — the opposite axis from every prior rune finding in this project (startipped-peak-rune-ramp, the free-2-Power floor of #44), which was about wanting MORE runes. 161.1.a keeps a rune on the board until it is Recycled, so a deck that recycles aggressively for Power stays light on runes as a side effect, turning all six on together. Protective Sands is a Battlefield: 485.5 has only 1 of the 3 you bring randomly selected for a Duel, so it is not guaranteed to be on the board even when it is in the deck — that caveat cannot be expressed by the predicate and belongs in a deck's own notes.

synergies.name: Rell attaches a cheap Equipment for free every time she attacks
synergies.why: "When I attack, you may play an Equipment with Energy cost no more than 2, ignoring its cost, [and] attach it to me" is a free PLAY-and-attach, not an Equip activation (818.1 does not apply to it — this is a Play Effect, 383.4.a, that happens to end in an attach), repeatable once per attack rather than once per game the way Weaponmaster's ETB is. Her own text caps the target at 2 Energy or less; the predicate cannot express a cost ceiling, so the list below is every [Equip] gear in the pool and a human has to read which ones clear her 2-Energy bar before valuing the pairing. 476.1's composition finding (#45) is what makes a cheap Equipment worth repeating here: attaching a second copy of the same effect text composes instead of stacking additively, so a Svellsongur-family target is worth more per attach than its Might bonus alone suggests.

synergies.name: Karma buffs a unit every time a [Vision] card recycles
synergies.why: Karma, Channeler's "When you recycle one or more cards to your Main Deck, buff a friendly unit" fires on the Main-Deck half of 416.1 (Recycling puts a card on the bottom of the corresponding deck), and [Vision]'s own reminder — 817.1.b, "functionally short for 'When this is played, predict'" — is exactly a look-and-optionally-recycle-to-the-Main-Deck trigger, one instance per [Vision] source (817.2, multiple instances trigger separately). No existing rule's textMatches reads the literal "[Vision]" bracket, so all 8 pool-wide [Vision] printings besides Karma herself fell through every prior synergy sweep.

synergies.name: Playing straight into an occupied enemy battlefield turns on Assault with no move
synergies.why: "You may play me to an occupied enemy battlefield" (Dauntless Vanguard; Deadbloom Predator and Rengar, Trophy Hunter's extended [Ambush] print the same permission) sets Attacker the instant the unit lands — 190.3.a.1 ("Units moving to or being played to a battlefield apply Contested status") and 464.2.c.1 ("The Attacker is the player whose unit(s) applied the Contested status") do not care whether the unit arrived by a move or by being played, and the Core Rules' own worked example under 359.3.f.1/f.2 confirms it in prose for a move ("A player moves Yasuo, Remorseful to an occupied enemy battlefield and initiates combat there"). trapping-grounds-excess-damage already established that [Assault] only pays while an Attacker designation exists (383.4.e, 807.1.d) — this pairing is that designation for free, with no Standard Move exhaust (420.3.a) and no Ganking needed, since the unit was never anywhere else on the board.

synergies.name: Profiteer moves the Empowered status instead of spending a card to grant it
synergies.why: "You may disempower something you control to empower a legend, unit, or gear" is Profiteer's own play effect, using "empower" as a plain verb rather than the [Empower] Activated Ability (827.1) — so sanction-empower-unit and hextech-formula-empower-gear, whose partner predicates require the card itself to carry [Empower], never reach the two legends that key off being empowered BY SOMEONE ELSE: Soul's Reflection and Matriarch of War, both "When you empower something else, empower me." 441.2 makes becoming Empowered by ANY game action a referenceable event regardless of source, so Profiteer's relay counts. 441.1.b caps the value: an already-Empowered legend gains nothing from a second empower, so the pairing is worth one relay per legend per time it is disempowered.

synergies.name: Any single buff turns on a static bonus that never has to stack
synergies.why: Two cards in the whole pool key a static bonus on simply CARRYING a buff rather than on granting or spending one — Wizened Elder ("an additional +1 Might") and Bilgewater Bully ("[Ganking]") — which every existing buff-family rule misses, since blade-dancer-buff-is-choosing, irelia-fervent-buff-is-choosing, wallop-buff-spend, sett-kingpin-mass-buff, albus-ferros-buff-bank and call-to-glory-buff-bank are all anchored on the GRANTER's own payoff for placing or spending a buff, not on a beneficiary that only wants to hold one. 702.3 ("There can only be one Buff on a Unit at a time") is exactly why this is a static bonus and never a stacking engine: any buff source in the pool, mass or single-target, turns it on for the one unit it targets. Call to Glory is reused as the anchor here rather than a fresh one, the same way SFD-180 already anchors two rules in this file.

synergies.name: A [Temporary] token's automatic death readies whatever watches the Beginning Phase
synergies.why: 816.1.b makes [Temporary] functionally "At the start of this permanent's controller's Beginning Phase, before scoring, kill this" — so every [Temporary] token's death happens inside that exact window. Shadow Watcher ("If a friendly unit died during your Beginning Phase this turn, I enter ready") and Shard of Undoing ("The first time a friendly unit dies during your Beginning Phase each turn...") are the only two cards in the pool that check specifically for a death IN that window rather than a death anywhere, and any of the pool's [Temporary]-token generators (Trevor Snoozebottom, Sprite Fountain, Sprite Mother, Bashful Bloom, plain Sprite tokens) supplies it for free every turn it is out. 383.1.b's own worked example is Shadow Watcher's neighbour Wraith of Echoes: if several [Temporary] deaths land at once, the controller of the checking ability picks one to serve as the trigger, which still satisfies Shadow Watcher's condition exactly once. LeBlanc, Everywhere at Once ("Your [Temporary] effects at my battlefield don't trigger") is the one card in the pool that turns this off — she suppresses the kill itself, so no death occurs for either payoff to see.

synergies.name: Two independent discounts on the same spell take it further than either alone

partner.textMatches: This spell's Energy cost is reduced

synergies.why: This is the Core Rules' own worked example, verbatim, at 356.4.e: "Eager Apprentice says 'While I'm at a battlefield, the Energy costs for spells you play is reduced by 1, to a minimum of 1.' A player who controls Eager Apprentice and a unit with 7 Might plays Sky Splitter, a spell that costs 8 Energy and says 'This spell's Energy cost is reduced by the highest Might among units you control.' That player can choose to apply Eager Apprentice's discount first, reducing Sky Splitter's Energy cost to 7, then apply Sky Splitter's discount, reducing its Energy cost to 0. If they applied these discounts in the other order, Sky Splitter's Energy cost would be 1." Sky Splitter is the only other card in the pool with a self-referential cost reduction (grepped for "this spell's ... cost is reduced"), so the pairing has exactly one partner — thin by the project's own standard, but the strongest possible citation: the rulebook uses these two cards, and no others, to teach the rule.

synergies.name: Soul Shepherd buffs every token unit the moment it lands, not just the ones she names
synergies.why: "Your token units have +1 Might" is a static, always-on grant that reads any token unit already on the board or entering later — unlike renata-industrialist-tokens, grand-plaza-unit-tokens and malzahar-token-fodder, which are about the act of PLAYING a token, this is the first anchor in the file for BUFFING a token once it exists, so it stacks on top of any of those three rather than competing with them. 185.2.b/185.2.d make a token unit a full unit for Might purposes, so the +1 applies without exception across the whole token-generator family.

synergies.name: Gemcraft Seer hands [Vision] to every friendly unit, not just Mechs
synergies.why: Forecaster ("Your Mechs have [Vision]") is the pool's narrow version of this static grant, restricted to a single tag; Gemcraft Seer's "Other friendly units have [Vision]" is the same mechanism (817.1's Triggered Ability keyword) generalized to ANY friendly unit entering the board, which is exactly what a unit-token generator produces in volume — every token that lands gets a free look-and-recycle (817.1.b) it would not otherwise carry. karma-channeler-vision-recycle is the downstream payoff for the [Vision] this creates; this rule is the upstream supply side.

synergies.name: A free, repeatable self-sacrifice outlet feeds the whole friendly-unit-dies family

partner.textMatches: friendly unit dies|unit you control dies

synergies.why: Malzahar, Fanatic's "Kill a friendly unit or gear, exhaust: Add [rainbow][rainbow]" is a mono-Mind, no-Energy sacrifice outlet — 185.2.d makes a token unit a legal cost payment, so cheap disposable fodder (Recruit, Gold, Sprite and other token bodies) feeds it without spending a card. Seven cards in the pool observe a friendly death with a payoff and were never grouped: Wraith of Echoes (draw), Spectral Centaur (+2 Might), Vanguard Helm (relay a buff), Viktor, Leader (a Recruit token), Altar of Memories (draw), Vicious Snapjaws (XP) and Shard of Undoing (forces an opponent kill). Two authoring traps from the Core Rules' own worked examples on this exact family: 383.1.b (Wraith of Echoes) — if several deaths land simultaneously, the WATCHING card's controller picks one to serve as the trigger, so simultaneous deaths from one sacrifice never grant more than one instance per watcher; and 383.2.c.2 (Viktor, Leader) — a watcher that dies in the SAME game action as the fodder never sees the death, since its trigger condition needs it "on the board immediately after" the death, not simultaneously with it.

synergies.name: Heimerdinger, Inventor gains every friendly exhaust ability on the board

excludes.why: "exhaust: Pay any amount of Energy to Add that much rainbow" has no cap per activation (per CLAUDE.md's own Ancient Henge note), so a second activation from the same instant is worth exactly zero — anything the second copy could convert, the first could have converted at once.
"exhaust: Pay any amount of rainbow to Add that much Energy" has no cap per activation, so a second simultaneous activation converts nothing a bigger single payment couldn't already.

synergies.why: "I have all exhaust abilities of all friendly legends, units, and gear" makes 377.1's colon syntax the whole predicate: any Activated Ability on a friendly legend, unit or gear becomes Heimerdinger's own, usable off his own exhaust and whatever else the cost asks for, without owning the source card or even having it on the board (Malzahar's kill-cost Power, Renata Mastermind's scoring exhaust, Vanguard Armory's three Recruits). Two things the list cannot show. 053.1 re-reads every "I"/"me" in the borrowed text as Heimerdinger, so a condition worded "while I'm at a battlefield" (377.2.b's own worked example is Ultrasoft Poro) becomes a condition on HIM, not on the card he copied it from (R30) — he must stand at a battlefield to use Renata's, Caitlyn's or Xerath's line even though they need not. And 383.1 is why this predicate stays clean of the readying family's traps: a "you may exhaust me to …" clause is a Triggered Ability (it fires off a trigger condition, not off being activated) and carries no colon, so it never matches and is never copied — only genuine Activated Abilities are.

synergies.name: Blade of the Ruined King pays its own Equip cost with any [Deathknell] card

excludes.why: "Your [Deathknell] effects trigger an additional time" only doubles OTHER permanents' Deathknells; he carries none of his own, so killing him with the Equip cost fires nothing.

synergies.why: 818.1.c.2 makes Equip a Cost — "Attach this gear to a unit you control" — and 377.1 reads the Blade's "[Equip] — 1 Order Power, Kill a friendly unit" as one combined cost paid to attach it, so the kill is EFFECT TEXT after the comma, not a targeted removal spell (416.3/203.3/185 never bite: 428.1 lets any friendly unit, including a token, pay it). Any [Deathknell] unit turns that cost into its own payoff on demand, in the same beat the Blade goes on: 808.1.a puts the Deathknell on the dying permanent and 808.1.d.2 chains it before the Blade's own Equip resolves. The Equip cost only spends a UNIT — the three gear carrying [Deathknell] in the raw grep (The Zero Drive, Sacred Shears, Sprite Fountain) never qualify, which is why the predicate is typed to units.

synergies.name: Heedless Resurrection pays its own additional cost with any [Deathknell] card

excludes.why: "Your [Deathknell] effects trigger an additional time" only doubles OTHER permanents' Deathknells; he carries none of his own, so killing him as the additional cost fires nothing.

synergies.why: Heedless Resurrection's additional cost — "kill a friendly unit" — is EFFECT text tied to a Cost (202/203.3), so any [Deathknell] unit turns the mandatory kill it needs to pay for anyway into a free extra trigger, on top of the reanimated body the spell hands back for no more Energy and no more Power than the one killed. 808.1.a puts the Deathknell on the dying permanent, and 808.1.d.2 chains it ahead of the spell's own resolution. Typed to units for the same reason as Blade of the Ruined King: the cost only spends a UNIT, so the three [Deathknell] gear in the pool never qualify.

synergies.name: Unforgiven's exhaust move fires a move trigger every turn for free
synergies.why: Unforgiven's legend ability — "2 Energy, exhaust: Move a friendly unit to or from its base" — is an effect Move (420.1), so it fires that unit's own move triggers and those of any Equipment attached to it (420.2.a), exactly like Ride the Wind and the other two move-effect anchors. The legend's cost carries an exhaust, so 315.1.b readies it once every Awaken: one free move trigger a turn for as long as Unforgiven is out, with no card spent. A recall is not a Move (456.1) and would not do this.

synergies.name: Grandmaster at Arms re-attaches an Equipment's per-event bonus to a new body for free every turn

partner.textMatches: attached to me this turn|[Ww]hen I (conquer|hold|attack|move|win a combat)

synergies.why: Grandmaster at Arms' second ability — "exhaust: Attach an attached Equipment you control to a unit you control" — carries no Energy, so once any of these fourteen is on somebody it can move to a fresh unit every turn for the price of the exhaust alone (818.1.c.2 makes Equip functionally "[Cost]: Attach this gear to a unit you control", and 434.1.f detaches it from the old unit automatically). Each of the fourteen grants a bonus keyed to something the WEARER does — conquer, hold, move, attack or defend, or (Brutalizer) simply having just been attached — so relaying it to a new unit each turn either spreads a one-shot buff across the board (Warmog's Armor, the two Gold-makers) or repoints a repeatable trigger at whichever body is best placed to fire it that turn (Recurve Bow, Forgefire Cape, Pendulum Blade). Two things the list cannot show. The legend's FIRST ability — "1 Energy, exhaust: attach a DETACHED Equipment" — is a separate, costed ability for the initial equip; only the free reattach is the engine here, so 315.1.b limits it to one reattachment a turn. And 434.1.c is why the moved bonus is live the instant it lands: the Top-Most Card's Rules Text already carries all Effect Text of everything Attached to it.

synergies.name: Kadregrin draws off the same Mighty count a mass buff or a big body maximizes
synergies.why: Kadregrin's "When you play me, draw 1 for each of your [Mighty] units" (708: 5+ Might) reads off the same count every other [Mighty]-keyed card in the pool cares about, and the walked entries use him on both sides of it. As a PAYOFF he pairs with anything that pushes bodies past the 5-Might line for free — Pridestalker's unconditional "give a unit +1 Might" on every unit play is the clean example, and Show of Strength (SFD-106) prints the identical "draw 1 for each of your [Mighty] units" line, so the two payoffs stack rather than compete. As a 9-Might BODY he is also fodder for cards that key off Mighty state or count rather than grant it — Sky Splitter's cost reduction reads "the highest Might among units you control", and Sacrifice and Sunken Temple both gate on a Mighty unit being present. The list mixes payoffs, triggers and thresholds on purpose: all nine observe the same 5-Might line, and a deck stacking several of them turns one buff or one big body into several simultaneous payoffs.

synergies.name: Undertitan pays for its own play with any effect that reveals from your own Main Deck

partner.textMatches: [Rr]eveal(s|ed|ing)? (the top|up to \d+ cards?|cards from|the top \d+ cards?)

excludes.why: "Each opponent reveals the top card of their Main Deck" reveals from the OPPONENT's deck, where Undertitan can never be sitting.
"reveal the top rune of your rune deck" reveals from the Rune Deck, not the Main Deck a unit card lives in.

synergies.why: Undertitan's "As I'm revealed from your deck, [Add] 2 Energy" is a zone-active Triggered Ability (385.2: abilities outside the board self-describe their context) that fires the instant ANY effect reveals from your own Main Deck (424.1/424.1.a.1 let a card reference the act of being revealed), whether or not it ends up played. The predicate is restricted to your OWN Main Deck on purpose: Blind Fury reveals the opponent's deck and Twisted Fate reveals the Rune Deck, and Undertitan can never be sitting in either. Left unplayed, a revealed Undertitan just recycles to the bottom (416.1.a) and can pay again the next time it surfaces, so every reveal-heavy card in the pool finances part of its own cost for free.

synergies.name: Black Market Broker turns every card in the [Hidden] package into a free Gold token

excludes.why: plays the [Hidden] card FROM HAND, ignoring its cost — 811.1.c.1 ("Hide is not a subset of Play") means that is not playing it from face down, so Black Market Broker never sees it.
watches for a card played from [Hidden]; it does not carry [Hidden] itself, so playing Ember Monk openly never triggers Black Market Broker.
returns [Hidden] cards from the trash and lets you hide cards for free; Guerilla Warfare itself carries no [Hidden] to be played from face down.
"Your opponents' [Hidden] cards can't be revealed here" is about the OPPONENT's hidden cards; Noxus Saboteur carries no [Hidden] of his own.
lets you hide a card for less; the legend itself has no [Hidden] to play from face down.

synergies.why: 811.1.c.3 — "Playing a card from facedown (or 'from Hidden') does open a chain" — is the event Black Market Broker's "When you play a card from face down" watches for, and every card carrying the [Hidden] keyword — including SFD-138 Windsinger, who prints it bracket-less as a registered upstream anomaly (docs/data-anomalies.md) but is a [Hidden] card in every rules sense (811.1) — is a card that CAN be that event: hide it for the printed rainbow cost, then play it later from Hidden, and the Broker mints a Gold gear token on top of whatever the card itself does. The predicate is deliberately about carrying [Hidden] on the card's OWN text, not about mentioning the keyword: five cards in the raw grep only reference [Hidden] cards in general (Ava Achiever plays one from hand, which 811.1.c.1 says is not the same event; Ember Monk, Noxus Saboteur, Guerilla Warfare and Swift Scout all talk about hiding or revealing without carrying [Hidden] themselves) and never trigger the Broker.

synergies.name: Flame Chompers turns any effect that discards your own hand into a body, free

excludes.why: "When you discard one or more cards, ready me" WATCHES for a discard; Jinx, Rebel never causes one herself, so she never puts Flame Chompers in the trash.
"When you discard me, you may pay to buff a unit" is a self-recursion payoff of the same shape as Flame Chompers, not a source that discards him.

synergies.why: "When you discard me, you may pay [Fury]: play me" is a Triggered Ability that self-describes its context (385.2) and evaluates its condition after the discard resolves (383.2.c) — it does not care WHY the card left the hand, only that it did, so every effect in the pool that discards a card from your own hand turns a 3-Energy 3-Might body sitting dead in your hand into a 1-Fury-Power body on the board. Repeatable sources (Square Up's [Repeat] discard, Master of Shadows' exhaust-discard) can rebuy him more than once a turn; a card that only discards on a Deathknell (Undercover Agent) or a move (Corrupt Enforcer, Hwei, Traveling Merchant) still finds him eventually. The predicate is restricted to effects that DISCARD — two cards in the raw grep only watch for a discard (Jinx, Rebel) or share Flame Chompers' own self-recursion shape (Mask Mother) without causing one.

synergies.name: Fae Dragon pays a Gold token for any card that spends a buff
synergies.why: "When you spend a buff, play a Gold gear token exhausted" is a Triggered Ability that watches the Buff status leave a unit (701, 702.2, 702.2.b), not who spends it or why, so Fae Dragon's own play trigger — buff up to four friendly units — feeds directly into every other card in the pool whose cost or effect spends one: Wallop and Call to Glory ignore their own cost for it, Kraken Hunter discounts itself per buff spent, Albus Ferros and Overt Operation spend several at once for runes or readies, Wildclaw Shaman and Monastery of Hirana spend one to ready or draw, and The Boss spends a dying unit's buff to save it. Each spend is a separate Gold, so Albus Ferros or Overt Operation spending several buffs in one resolution mints one Gold per buff, not one for the card.

synergies.name: Leona, Zealot turns any stun into near-lethal removal

excludes.why: it does not stun anything — "When you stun an enemy unit, ready me" is a second payoff for the stun, so it wants the same third card Leona does rather than pairing with her.
same shape — "When you [Stun] an enemy unit at a battlefield, you may move me there" pays for a stun somebody else provides; she is not a source.
"When you stun one or more enemy units, buff a friendly unit" is the same shape as Eclipse Herald and Vex, Mocking: a payoff that watches for a stun rather than a source that provides one.

synergies.why: Leona's "Stunned enemy units here have -8 Might, to a minimum of 1" makes 423.1.c matter more than 423.1.b: a stunned unit still needs damage equal to its full CURRENT Might to die, so any stun landed at her battlefield collapses the defender to as low as 1 Might before combat damage is even assigned. 423.1.a.1 caps the family (a Stunned Unit cannot be Stunned again) and 423.1.a.2 clears the state only at end-of-turn cleanup, so one stun a turn per unit is the ceiling regardless of how many sources are stacked. Two entries in the raw grep only watch for a stun instead of causing one — same shape as radiant-dawn-stun-buff's own excludes, plus Radiant Dawn herself for the identical reason.

synergies.name: Solari Chief turns a second stun source into an outright kill

excludes.why: it does not stun anything — "When you stun an enemy unit, ready me" is a second payoff for the stun, so it wants the same third card Solari Chief does rather than pairing with him.
same shape — "When you [Stun] an enemy unit at a battlefield, you may move me there" pays for a stun somebody else provides; she is not a source.
"When you stun one or more enemy units, buff a friendly unit" is the same shape as Eclipse Herald and Vex, Mocking: a payoff that watches for a stun rather than a source that provides one.

synergies.why: Solari Chief's own play trigger — "Choose an enemy unit. If it is stunned, kill it. Otherwise, stun it." — is itself a conditional stun/kill, so any OTHER stun source in the pool that reaches the same unit first turns his second half into an outright kill instead of a second stun (423.1.a.1 forbids stunning an already-stunned unit anyway, so the card's own text anticipates exactly this). 423.1.a.2 clears the state only at end-of-turn cleanup, so the two stuns have to land in the same turn. Two entries in the raw grep only watch for a stun instead of causing one, plus Radiant Dawn for the same reason.

synergies.name: Ava Achiever plays any [Hidden] card from hand for 1 Mind Power

excludes.why: watches for a card played from [Hidden]; it does not carry [Hidden] itself.
returns [Hidden] cards from the trash and discounts hiding; it carries no [Hidden] of its own.
"Your opponents' [Hidden] cards can't be revealed here" is about the opponent's hidden cards; he carries none himself.
discounts hiding a card; the legend itself has no [Hidden] to play.
"When you play this from face down" needs the card to actually come from Hidden — Ava Achiever plays it FROM HAND instead, so the attach trigger never fires.
"When you play me from face down on your turn" is the same trap: played from hand, her move-in trigger never fires.
"When you play me from face down" — played from hand instead, the Empower option never triggers.

synergies.why: Ava Achiever's "When I attack, you may pay 1 Mind Power to play a card with [Hidden] from your hand, ignoring its cost" turns every card in the [Hidden] package into a flat 1-Power play, whatever it prints — 811.1.a scopes the keyword to Spells, Units and Gear (SFD-138 Windsinger counts too, despite printing Hidden bracket-less — a registered upstream anomaly, docs/data-anomalies.md — since her "When you play me" trigger has no from-face-down gate to lose), so a 6-Energy [Hidden] spell and a 1-Energy one cost the same off her attack trigger. Two shapes in the raw grep do not belong. Four cards only mention [Hidden] in their own text without carrying it (the same four Black Market Broker's rule excludes for the same reason). And 811.1.c.1 ("Hide is not a subset of Play") is why three more are only PARTIALLY live here: Edge of Night, Evelynn, Entrancing and Tornado Warrior each gate their real payoff on being played FROM FACE DOWN specifically, and Ava Achiever's ability plays the card from hand instead — the card still lands on the board, but the attach/move/empower bonus that makes it worth naming here never fires.

synergies.name: Show of Strength draws off the same Mighty count Kadregrin does
synergies.why: Show of Strength prints the identical "Draw 1 for each of your [Mighty] units" Kadregrin carries, as a [Reaction] spell instead of a unit's play trigger — so it stacks with him rather than competing, and it can be cast on the opponent's turn once your board is already built. Same family (708: 5+ Might) and same two-sided pairing as kadregrin-mighty-payoff: a mass-buff enabler (Pridestalker) that pushes bodies over the line feeds it directly, and it also reads off the same count as the threshold cards (Sacrifice, Sunken Temple) that only need a Mighty unit to be present.

synergies.name: Pridestalker pushes every unit you play toward the 5-Might line, for free
synergies.why: "When you play a unit, give a unit +1 Might this turn" has no cost and no "may" — 709 makes becoming Mighty an event that fires only the moment Might crosses from below 5 to 5+, so a body sitting at 4 only needs this ONE buff to cross it, on every single unit play. That is the enabler half of the [Mighty] family: Kadregrin and Show of Strength both draw off the resulting count, and the threshold cards (Sacrifice, Sunken Temple, Unsung Hero) only need the crossing to have happened once. The buff itself is a continuous modifier granted by card text, not a 702 counter, so it never collides with 702.3's one-buff cap.

synergies.name: Isolate empties a battlefield for a card that walks straight onto it

partner.textMatches: play me to an open battlefield|played to open battlefields

synergies.why: Isolate moves the garrison's last body to its own base, and 323.6 strips the opponent's Control the moment it leaves — 170.11.c defines "open" as unoccupied AND uncontrolled, both of which are now true, so 355.2.b's small family of cards that may be PLAYED to a battlefield they do not already occupy can walk straight in from hand. 190.3.a.1 (not 450) is the citation for the played half — units "moving to or being played to" a battlefield apply Contested. The predicate is narrow on purpose: 449 governs a MOVE onto an open battlefield, a different action from being PLAYED there, so Bard, Mercurial (which moves units it already controls) is not a match — he needs the board empty of everyone, not merely open, and grants no play permission at all.

synergies.name: Curator of the Sands readies runes off any 7-Energy unit or gear, printed cost only
synergies.why: "When you play a unit, gear, or activated ability with Energy cost 7 or more, you may exhaust me to ready up to 2 runes" is the same 206 reading lady-of-luminosity-expensive-spells stands on — 206's own worked example IS this family (Lux, Illuminated), so a discount, a Hidden play at 811.1.b's 0 Energy, or any other reduction never switches the trigger off; only the PRINTED cost is read. One threshold higher than Lady of Luminosity's 5, and on the other two card types instead of spells. The third leg of Curator's own text — an activated ability costing 7+ Energy — has no printed-cost field at card level (`minEnergy` reads the CARD's own cost, not an ability's), so it cannot be represented here and is not covered by this rule's partner list.

synergies.name: Jax, Unrelenting draws a card for every Equipment attach, on top of the Weaponmaster discount
synergies.why: "When you attach an Equipment to me, you may pay 1 Energy to draw 1" is a Triggered Ability that fires on the Attach action itself (818.1 makes Equip an Activated Ability that performs it, and any other effect that attaches a card counts too), with no cap and no exhaust — every [Equip] activation and every [Quick-Draw] auto-attach draws a card if you spend the Energy, and 434.1.g's only carve-out (attaching a card to its CURRENT Top-Most Card does nothing) never applies to a fresh attach. Same predicate and shape as aphelios-equipment-attach, a second anchor on the same family: any Equipment in the pool works, and a detach-then-reattach loop (Serrated Dirk's own Reaction) or a [Weaponmaster] re-equip both trigger it again.

synergies.name: Marai Spire discounts every [Repeat] cost in the list by 1 Energy

excludes.why: its [Repeat] cost is a rune only ("[Repeat] rune_chaos") — no Energy for a "1 Energy less" discount to reduce.
its [Repeat] cost is "Discard 1" — no Energy component, so the discount has nothing to apply to.

synergies.why: "While you control this battlefield, friendly [Repeat] costs cost 1 Energy less" reads the PLURAL "costs", so a spell with more than one [Repeat] instance in its own text (Curtain Call prints three) gets the discount on EACH one, not once per spell. Two caveats the list cannot show: 190.1 means the battlefield has to be taken before its text does anything, and 485.5 draws it at random from the three a player brings, so it is not guaranteed to be on the board even when it is in the deck. Excluded are the two [Repeat] costs printed with no Energy component at all (a rune, a discard) — a "1 Energy less" discount has nothing to reduce on either.

synergies.name: Lee Sin, Ascetic breaks the one-buff cap for any repeatable buff source
synergies.why: 702.3 caps every unit in the pool at ONE buff at a time (702.3.a: a second buff offered to an already-buffed unit is simply not placed), which is why buffs elsewhere are a status to spend, not a resource to stack — Lee Sin, Ascetic's own "I can have any number of buffs" is the pool's one printed exception. That makes any REPEATABLE buff source worth stacking on him specifically: an exhaust-cost activated ability readies every Awaken (315.1.b), so Blind Monk's legend ability and Arena Bar's gear ability both add a fresh +1 Might to him every turn instead of fizzling against the cap. The list is small on purpose — a one-shot buff (a play trigger, a spell) only ever gives him the one it would give anyone else; it is the REPEATABLE sources that turn his exception into unbounded Might.

synergies.name: Bewitching Spirit strips a hand card every time a friendly unit-bounce effect fires

excludes.why: "return a friendly gear to its owner's hand" only ever moves gear — Bewitching Spirit is a unit, so this can never bounce him for a replay.

synergies.why: "When you play me, choose a player. They discard 1" fires again every time Bewitching Spirit is replayed, and 124 makes each replay a new object, so any effect that returns a FRIENDLY UNIT to its owner's hand — Retreat, Pack of Wonders, Grim Apothecary's own play trigger, Bloodharbor Ripper's exhaust, Mesmerize's first mode — buys another discard for a card already spent once. "Choose a player" lets the discard land on either hand: aimed at yourself it feeds Flame Chompers or any other discard-triggered recursion; aimed at an opponent it strips their hand one card at a turn. The predicate is typed to bounces of a UNIT specifically: Legion Quartermaster's near-identical wording only returns a friendly GEAR, so it can never pick Bewitching Spirit up.

synergies.name: Chem-Baroness stacks Gold producers into a resource package, independent of Industrialist
synergies.why: Chem-Baroness is herself a Gold producer ("you may exhaust me to play a Gold gear token exhausted"), so stacking her with the pool's other Gold producers is additive ramp rather than an amplifying interaction the way `renata-industrialist-tokens` reads the SAME partner list for a different reason (making the tokens usable the turn they land). 184.1 lets a token's own text override the default it would otherwise get; a Gold gear token's default under 149.1 ("Gear enter play Ready") is overridden to exhausted by every producer's own printed wording, and it readies on its controller's own next Awaken (315.1.b). Each Gold is worth exactly 1 rainbow Power when sacrificed (`UNL-T05 Gold`'s own "Kill this, exhaust: Add rainbow"), so N producers in one turn is N delayed Power a turn later — no card in the pool reads "for each Gold gear token you control," so the stack never scales beyond that flat sum. Chem-Baroness's own second clause is the one thing that changes the arithmetic: "While your score is within 3 points of the Victory Score, your Gold [Add] an additional 1 Energy" turns every Gold made from that point on into 1 Power AND 1 Energy at once, so the value of stacking producers rises specifically in the turns right before Victory Score, not before.

synergies.name: A spell replayed from the trash doubles a "when you play a spell" payoff for free

No rule in the pool currently anchors on "when you play a spell" at all — this is the first. `SFD-140 Fizz, Trickster` and `OGN-112 Kai'Sa, Evolutionary` both let you play a spell straight out of the trash, ignoring its Energy cost, which is a second "you play a spell" event off a single card already spent — Ravenbloom grows twice off one casting instead of needing a second copy in hand. A [Flow] spell does the same thing to itself: 829.1.b lets its owner "play this from your trash for its flow cost," so every [Flow] spell in the list is a second trigger waiting in the graveyard once it is there, though on its own timeline rather than guaranteed the same turn. 829.1.b.1 banishes it after that replay, so this is one extra trigger per copy, never a loop.

"[Buff] all units here" — 702.3 caps every one of them at one buff, so unless a buff was deliberately spent between the two Beginning Phases the second one lands on already-buffed bodies and does nothing.

synergies.why: 734–738 insert the Additional Turn immediately after the current one, with no opponent turn between, so its own Beginning Phase (315.2) Holds your battlefields again (469.2's "did not yet Score this turn" resets on the new turn) and every Hold Effect on them fires a second time — this is issue #155's Candidate 1 (`power-nexus-sentinel` + Time Warp): the entry's own `terminatesIn` already named the extra turn as the missing piece before this rule existed to say so structurally. `time-warp-once-per-turn` (same anchor) catches a different trigger shape — cards worded "At the start of your Beginning Phase" or "at the end of your turn" — while this rule catches the separately-defined Hold Trigger category (383.4.d) blue-sentinel-hold already reads the pool for; the two lists do not overlap. Unlike Blue Sentinel's simultaneous double, the two firings sit on different turns, so a fixed-target trigger is only a no-op when nothing changed the board state in between — most of the excludes below are one-shot cards that leave the board on their first firing, not universal no-ops.

synergies.name: Peak Guardian turns on every "while I'm buffed" static in one play
synergies.why: Peak Guardian's own trigger — "buff me. Then, if I am at a battlefield, buff all other friendly units there" — hands out a buff to every body standing with him for one card, no Energy sink or spell needed. The two cards that key a static bonus on simply CARRYING a buff (`OGN-065 Wizened Elder`, "an additional +1 Might"; `OGN-125 Bilgewater Bully`, "[Ganking]") turn on the instant they are at his battlefield when he lands — cheaper than `call-to-glory-buff-bank`'s route, which needs a spell in hand for each activation. 702.3 ("There can only be one Buff on a Unit at a time") is why this is a flat one-time switch, not a stacking engine: Peak Guardian's own mass buff and any later Call to Glory compete for the same single buff slot on each body, they do not add.

synergies.name: Bloodharbor Ripper replays a unit's play effect every turn for one Energy, no card spent

excludes.why: the predicate caught "play a non-token gear" in his trigger condition; his play effect readies something, it puts nothing on the board.

synergies.why: "1 Energy, exhaust: Return a friendly unit at a battlefield to its owner's hand. Play a Gold gear token exhausted." is an ACTIVATED ability, not a spent card, so unlike `retreat-replays-a-body` (one bounce per copy, 3 copies a game by 103.2.b) this is a bounce-and-replay every turn 315.1.b readies him — the same body's play effect fires again for a flat 1 Energy, plus a Gold on top. The one restriction Retreat does not share: the target must already be AT A BATTLEFIELD, so the bounced unit has to walk there again after replaying (144.4.a), which the entry states as the cost this line pays that Retreat's does not.

synergies.name: Sprite Queen feeds any "friendly unit dies" payoff for free, every Beginning Phase

synergies.why: "When you play me or at the start of your Beginning Phase, play a ready 3 Might Sprite unit token with [Temporary] to your base" mints a body that 816.1.b guarantees dies before scoring THAT SAME turn — a repeatable friendly death with no cost, no card spent past the one copy, and no activation to remember. `malzahar-fanatic-friendly-death-payoff` (same partner list) is anchored on an ACTIVATED kill outlet that costs a card in hand to feed each time; Sprite Queen is the free, automatic alternative — the death happens whether or not you want it to, on schedule, every turn she is on the board. 185 / 186.1 still apply: the Sprite is a token, so nothing that recycles or reanimates from the trash ever sees it.

synergies.name: Shrinking the defender is the other route to excess damage

excludes.why: its trigger is the ENEMY attacking a battlefield you control, i.e. you are defending, and the -1 Might lasts only that turn; Tryndamere's own threshold checks a conquer after YOUR attack, on your own turn — the two events are never the same combat, and the debuff has already expired by the time you attack back.

synergies.why: `trapping-grounds-excess-damage` (same excess-damage family: OGN-034, SFD-120, UNL-018, UNL-187, UNL-188, UNL-217) already reads the pool for the OTHER lever — raising the attacker's own Might with [Assault]. This is the mirror: 465.2.c.4 forbids assigning a unit more damage than the minimum needed to kill it, and that minimum is the defender's CURRENT Might (143.2.a, 143.2.b), so lowering the defender's Might by any amount lowers the bill and raises the same attacker's excess by the same amount. `UNL-198 Moonfall` drags the target onto the attacker's battlefield and shrinks it in the same card; `OGN-116 Thousand-Tailed Watcher` shrinks every enemy unit present for the rest of the turn on an ETB. 477.3.b caps a FLOORED reduction ("to a minimum of 1") at the floor, so the bill only drops to 1, never to 0 — 143.2.a still needs nonzero damage to kill, so a 1-Might body still costs 1.

synergies.name: A big flat Might boost is the cheapest way to discount Sky Splitter
synergies.why: "This spell's Energy cost is reduced by the highest Might among units you control" reads the board at the moment it is cast (356's discount timing), not a snapshot from earlier — so a body already sitting at high Might is worth less than a body a same-turn buff has just pushed there, since the buff itself does not cost the spell anything. `eager-apprentice-sky-splitter-order-matters` already reads OGN-116's -3 (a REMOVAL setup, cheapening the KILL, not the CAST); this rule is the other half — cheapening the CAST itself with a body already at 5+ Might. 356.4.c.1 lets a player apply this discount whenever it is most favorable relative to any other cost reduction on the same spell.

synergies.name: Master of Shadows empowers off any card that banishes one of your own

excludes.why: her own text only discounts OTHER [Flow] spells you replay — she carries no [Flow] herself and banishes nothing, so she never fires the trigger, only makes someone else's replay cheaper.
"banish an enemy unit" — the predicate's "a" matched inside "an", but the card it names is never one you own; this banish is never yours.

A second false-positive shape, caught only by reading the whole list: 416.1.c makes each player recycle cards to their OWN Main Deck, so an effect that forces an opponent to recycle their own hand or trash card never touches Karma's controller's deck at all.

The one exclude, Walking Roost, makes the OPPONENT play the token, so it is never Lillia's own controller doing the playing. Her static grant — "Your token units have [Tank]" — is the assignment restriction of 815.1.b / 815.1.c.2 (a unit without Tank is an invalid assignment until every Tank body has lethal damage assigned), which is exactly why she is anti-synergic with the whole Grand Plaza family: those lines need seven token bodies to SURVIVE to the Beginning Phase, and Tank guarantees hers die first.

synergies.name: Shard of Undoing wants a scheduled friendly death — in practice, [Temporary]

excludes.why: its own [Temporary] is on the GEAR (Petricite Monument itself), never on a friendly unit.
"[Temporary] (If this is unattached, kill it...)" applies to the gear (Spinning Axe) itself, not to a unit.

its own [Temporary] is on the GEAR (Sumpworks Map itself), never on a friendly unit.

The fourteen partners below either mint a token that already carries [Temporary] (the Sprite and Reflection families) or hand the keyword to an existing friendly body (Last Stand, Shadow's Call, Fading Memories — whose "a unit at a battlefield" can be pointed at your own). Keeper of Masks is worth two: 185.3.a.2 and 477.1.b.1.a make [Temporary] a copyable trait, so his two Reflection copies die alongside him. Eight excludes split three ways: four cards put [Temporary] on a GEAR rather than a unit; two only READ an existing [Temporary] state instead of granting it; and LeBlanc, Everywhere at Once actively disables the mechanism (R10 = A) — the one genuine anti-synergy in the raw list.

Same 24-card cause family as flame-chompers-discard-family, sharing both of its exclusions for the identical reason: Mask Mother and Flame Chompers each watch a discard of themselves rather than causing one.
